source.author: lucan
source.text: Inde ubi nulla data est miscendi copia Martis, Paullatim cadit ira ferox, mentesque tepescunt; Saucia maiores animos ut pectora gestant, Dum dolor est ictusque recens, et mobile nervis Conamen calidus praebet cruor, ossaque nondum Adduxere cutem: si conscius ensis adacti Stat victor, tenuitque manus, tunc frigidus artus Alligat atque animum subducto robore torpor, Postquam sicca rigens astrinxit vulnera sanguis.
source.text_original: Inde ubi nulla data est miscendi copia Martis, / Paullatim cadit ira ferox, mentesque tepescunt; / Saucia maiores animos ut pectora gestant, / Dum dolor est ictusque recens, et mobile nervis / Conamen calidus praebet cruor, ossaque nondum / Adduxere cutem: si conscius ensis adacti / Stat victor, tenuitque manus, tunc frigidus artus / Alligat atque animum subducto robore torpor, / Postquam sicca rigens astrinxit vulnera sanguis.
source.text_english: Then, when no chance was given to mix in the battle of Mars, the fierce anger gradually falls, and the minds grow warm. Wounded hearts carry greater spirits while the pain and the recent blow remain, and while hot blood supplies a strength that moves the sinews and the bones have not yet drawn the skin tight; if the conscious sword of the thrust stands victorious and the hand has held firm, then cold numbness binds the limbs and torpor, with strength withdrawn, seizes the spirit, after the dry blood has stiffened and closed the wounds.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: non nuntia tantum fama refert: ipsum iuvenem tam saeva gementem, ipsum ego, cum serus fessos sopor alligat artus, aspicio; lacera assiduis namque illius umbra questibus et magni numen maris excitat Helle.
reuse.text_original: non nuntia tantum / fama refert: ipsum iuvenem tam saeva gementem, / ipsum ego, cum serus fessos sopor alligat artus, / aspicio; lacera assiduis namque illius umbra / questibus et magni numen maris excitat Helle.
reuse.text_english: Report does not bring only tidings: I myself behold the young man, groaning so fiercely, I myself, when late sleep binds weary limbs, do I see him; for Helle, torn by constant laments, and the divinity of the great sea, rouses his shade.
